hero.headline: Specialist behaviour support for children, teenagers and adults from everyday challenges to complex situations.
hero.sub: Behaviour support, regulation, and carer coaching for Child Safety, Youth Justice, and out-of-home care across the Sunshine Coast. Trauma-informed, evidence-based, and built for the realities of statutory work.

why.title: Why work with us
why.card1Body: More than a decade supporting children, young people, and adults across Child Safety, Youth Justice, residential care, schools, and community settings.
why.card2Body: We work where behaviours occur in placements, schools, and community settings, providing practical support alongside the people working with the individual every day.
why.card3Body: Our approach is informed by an understanding of trauma, attachment, and lived experience, helping create strategies that are realistic, consistent, and sustainable.
why.card4Body: Our focus is on strategies that can be used in everyday situations. The goal is to provide support that leads to meaningful change, not reports that sit on a shelf.

audiences.title: Who we work with
audiences.row1Help: Practical, in-the-moment strategies for the everyday challenges of raising or caring for a child whose behaviour feels hard to navigate.
audiences.row2Help: Direct, age-appropriate support for young people learning to regulate big feelings, navigate change, and build skills that hold up at home and school.
audiences.row3Help: Behaviour support shaped around your goals and routines — focused on what makes daily life work, not what's written in a manual.
audiences.row4Help: Consultation, planning, and in-classroom strategies for students whose behaviour is making the school day harder than it needs to be.
audiences.row5Help: Coaching, supervision, and shared planning so the team around a young person can hold the work — not just file it.
audiences.row6Help: Specialist behaviour support delivered under your NDIS plan, with reports and reviews that meet plan-manager and Quality and Safeguards Commission requirements.

services.title: Practical, hands-on services
services.card1Body: Functional Behaviour Assessments, Behaviour Support Plans, and practical strategies tailored to the individual's needs.
services.card2Body: Individualised support and intervention strategies that build skills, confidence, and positive outcomes.
services.card3Body: Practical guidance to help families and carers respond consistently and confidently to challenging behaviours.
services.card4Body: Behaviour support and capacity-building strategies that promote independence and participation in everyday life.
services.card5Body: Collaboration with teachers and support staff to develop consistent approaches across educational settings.
services.card6Body: Support for individuals, families, or professionals who need expert advice or are unsure where to begin.

founder.quote: I started The Guidance Co. to do the work properly, supporting the young people the system finds hardest to hold and the families, carers, and professionals working alongside them.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1Question: Are you NDIS registered and aligned to the PBS Capability Framework?
faq.q1Answer: Yes. We're an NDIS-registered behaviour support provider operating under the PBS Capability Framework, with current Working with Children Check and Blue Card credentials.
faq.q2Question: Do you accept Child Safety and Youth Justice brokerage?
faq.q2Answer: Yes. We invoice CSO and YJ brokerage directly, alongside NDIS plan-managed and self-managed funding. We can also work on direct-billed engagements outside the NDIS where required.
faq.q3Question: How do you work with residential care and kinship placements?
faq.q3Answer: In the placement. We coach the team carrying the young person — residential workers, kinship and foster carers — and stay long enough for the regulation and behaviour strategies to land in practice, not just on paper.
faq.q4Question: What ages and order types do you work with?
faq.q4Answer: Children and young people 4–18 on Child Protection Orders, Youth Justice orders, and at the edge of statutory involvement. We work across short-term, long-term, kinship, foster, and residential placement types.
faq.q5Question: What's your turnaround on assessments and reports?
faq.q5Answer: Most functional behaviour assessments turn around inside 4–6 weeks from referral. Court and review reports are scoped to deadline at the scoping conversation — we don't take work we can't deliver on time.
faq.q6Question: Do you provide reports for court, case plans, and reviews?
faq.q6Answer: Yes. We provide functional behaviour reports, PBS plans, restrictive-practice reviews, and supporting documentation for case planning, ongoing reviews, and Children's Court matters where appropriate.
faq.q7Question: Do you offer secondary consultation between formal sessions?
faq.q7Answer: Yes — and it's often the most useful part of an engagement. Teams can call between sessions for a 15-minute consult on what's coming up. It's built into the engagement scope, not billed separately.
